01.r: To announce the year publicly, as a herald does.
01.n: Abbott-Smith: 'to be a herald, to proclaim', citing this verse and the one before. It continues the list of what the speaker was sent to do.

02.r: A year marked out by God.
02.n: Abbott-Smith gives its proper sense as 'a cycle of time', then simply 'a year'. Coming after the 'release' of Luke 4:18, it is a reasonable reading to hear the year of release, the jubilee, behind it; the Greek itself says only 'year'.

03.r: The year belongs to God, who grants it.
03.n: There is no article in the Greek. Abbott-Smith notes that the Septuagint uses this word chiefly for יהוה, God's name.

04.r: A year of God's favour, gladly received.
04.n: A verbal adjective from δέχομαι, to receive or welcome; Abbott-Smith gives 'acceptable', and notes that the Septuagint uses it chiefly for Hebrew רָצוֹן. The BSB's 'year of the Lord's favor' likely reflects that Hebrew word's sense of favour; our 'welcome' keeps the Greek link to receiving.
